focus: Frontier node F-2-010 (depth 2, scope .skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/runtime/lib/run-record.ts, status-index.ts, switches.ts): Which OpenBot routine guardrails, the 20-enabled cap and failure-streak auto-off, belong in run records and the status index for a small team?
noveltyJustification: 6 of 8 findings were fully new and 2 synthesized the guardrails onto existing run-record and switch surfaces.
keyQuestions: Which OpenBot routine guardrails, the 20-enabled cap and failure-streak auto-off, belong in run records and the status index for a small team?
answeredQuestions: Which OpenBot routine guardrails, the 20-enabled cap and failure-streak auto-off, belong in run records and the status index for a small team?
ruledOut: Adding a fatigue counter to each BOT.md definition
Reusing the drain backoff as the fatigue rule
Making the fatigue stop a silent disable

label: OpenBot caps a person at 20 enabled routines because a conversation is an easy place to accumulate standing work without noticing, and switching one off frees a slot.

OpenBot's fatigue rule posts one message on the first failure after a success, switches the routine off after ten consecutive failures with a second final message, and resets the count when a person turns it back on.
Skilled bots has neither a per-bot failure streak nor an enabled-bot cap; the only related backoff is the drain job's setup-fault backoff, which protects the drain rather than a bot's schedule.
The status index already stores one row per run with botId and exitReason, built only from run records and needs-you items, so a failure streak is a query over existing rows rather than a new store.
The needs-you store models one durable operator item per run and the delivery resolver routes per-channel entries, so a switched-off-after-N-failures notice can reuse both.

The stop-switch layer stores only setAt for disabled and paused, so an automatic fatigue stop is indistinguishable from a person's disable; it needs a reason or a distinct kind so bots enable can tell them apart.

The smallest change is a post-run check that counts the last ten terminal run rows for the bot from the status index, and at ten sets a disabled switch with reason failure-streak and writes one needs-you item; bots enable clears it and resets the count. Size S, low risk.

The 20-enabled cap belongs at bots enable and bots schedule install: count enabled definitions or installed schedules and refuse the 21st with a named reason, preserving OpenBot's protection against unnoticed accumulation at size S and low risk.
